claims.statement: The supported local environment requires Python 3.14 and configures uv to use a managed interpreter, while the reader-install workflow exercises the documented installation on Linux x86_64, Apple Silicon macOS, and native Windows and explicitly asserts that Intel macOS remains Docker-only because torch has no compatible distribution.
The main ml4t image creates a managed Python 3.14 environment at /opt/ml4t; amd64 uses CUDA PyTorch and a CUDA-built lock-selected LightGBM, while arm64 uses CPU PyTorch and wheel LightGBM.

Compose uses the same main image for CPU and GPU services, with the GPU profile adding NVIDIA device passthrough, and maps the repository and writable data root to /app and /data with ML4T_PATH and ML4T_DATA_PATH aligned to those mounts.

The amd64-only py312 image isolates Python-3.14-incompatible signature, gensim, and Torch/CUDA workloads, and runs tfcausalimpact in a separate /opt/bsts interpreter because its NumPy 1/pandas constraints conflict with the default py312 NumPy 2 signature stack.

The benchmark environment supports storage and database comparisons on amd64 and arm64 without ArcticDB, while benchmark-full adds the x86-only ArcticDB path and Compose provides TimescaleDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, QuestDB, and InfluxDB services.

The RAPIDS environment is a locally built, single-purpose amd64/NVIDIA Python 3.12 image that preserves the compiled RAPIDS base stack, selectively takes compatible packages from the root lock, and builds the lock-selected LightGBM with CUDA; it is not part of the published image set.
Neo4j-dependent Chapter 23 tests run against a health-checked pinned Neo4j service and execute graph producers before consumers because notebooks share graph state.

Container dependency installation derives pinned constraints from uv.lock, and CI checks installed distributions against the lock while honoring explicit overrides and special-build carve-outs rather than allowing ordinary packages to drift above or below the locked version.
Ruff is exactly pinned across the project dev extra, pre-commit hooks, CI lint commands, and uv.lock, and tests fail when these surfaces diverge.

Installation verification treats concrete ML4T subpackages, repository imports, startup-hook/path behavior, plotting configuration, and other runtime checks as required, reports missing GPU support as a skip, treats Docker-profile extras as optional, and exits nonzero only when required checks fail.

The container smoke workflow runs on relevant pull requests, weekly, and manually, executes the reader's Compose download path, and verifies both that /data is writable and that the downloaded artifact appears on the host side of the bind mount.

The main test workflow is path-filtered for pull requests but runs the full shipped matrix on main pushes, weekly schedules, Docker Publish completion, and requested full runs; it includes always-on lint, guards, native unit tests, Docker chapter/case matrices, py312 routing, and Neo4j routing, while its benchmark job is currently disabled.
The manual full-test workflow is the broad release gate for chapter notebooks, nine case-study pipelines, and—when scope is all—the py312 compatibility set.

The weekly external workflow runs weekly-tier notebooks and live free-provider drift tests on Monday, manages per-notebook/source issues from JUnit results, and restores its pinned Hugging Face cache on Wednesday and Friday to prevent inactivity eviction.

The Docker publish workflow rebuilds affected main, py312, and benchmark images on relevant main changes, tags, or manual requests; for the main image it publishes architecture-specific digests, verifies each digest with the reader installation gate before moving tags, then smoke-tests the published multi-architecture manifest.
